'''''Celosia argentea''''', commonly known as the '''plumed cockscomb''' or '''silver cock's comb''',<ref name=usda>{{cite web|title=''Celosia argentea'' L.|url=http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=CECR2|work=USDA|access-date=13 December 2013}}</ref> is a [[herb]]aceous [[plant]] of [[tropical]] origin in the family [[Amaranthaceae]]<ref name="MBG">{{cite web |title=''Celosia argentea'' (Plumosa Group) 'New Look' |url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=267315 |website=Plant Finder |date=n.d. |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |access-date=4 January 2023 }}</ref> from [[tropical Africa]].<ref>https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:316350-2</ref> The plant is known for its very bright colors. In India and China it is known as a troublesome [[weed]].<ref name=cytol>{{cite journal|last=Grant|first=William F.|title=A Cytological Study of ''Celosia argentea'', ''C. argentea'' var. ''cristata'', and Their Hybrids|journal=Botanical Gazette|volume=115|issue=4|year=1954|publisher=The University of Chicago Press|pages=323–336|jstor=2473317|doi=10.1086/335831|s2cid=85012309}}</ref>

==Description==
''Celosia argentea'' is a tender [[annual plant|annual]] that is often grown in [[garden]]s, it can also grow [[perennial plant|perennially]].<ref name="EGPT">{{cite web |title=''Celosia argentea'' |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/celosia-argentea/ |date=n.d. |website=North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |publisher=[[North Carolina State University]] |access-date=4 January 2023 }}</ref> It blooms in mid-spring to summer. The plant exhibits [[Polyploidy|dodecaploidy]].

The flowers are tiny and [[hermaphrodite]], they are packed in narrow, pyramidal, plume-like [[pseudanthium|heads]] {{convert|4-10|in|cm}} long with vivid colors including shades of orange, red, purple, yellow and cream.<ref name="MBG"/>

It is [[plant propagation|propagated]] by black seeds. The seeds come in [[capsule (fruit)|capsule]]s;<ref name="MBG"/> they are extremely small, up to 43,000 seeds per ounce.<ref name=davegar>{{cite web|title=Cockscomb|url=http://davesgarden.com/guides/pf/go/212/|work=Dave's Garden|accessdate=13 December 2013}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
A plant of tropical origin, they grow best in full sunlight and should be placed in a well-drained area. Full sunlight means they should get at least 8 hours of direct sunlight. For healthy growth plant them in the area where they get early morning sunlight and afternoon shade. In the afternoon the sunlight is mostly harsh especially in hot summer. Afternoon shade will save the plant from excessive heat.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-12-19|title=How to grow colorful celosia: The complete guide|url=https://shinyplant.com/celosia/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121222440/https://shinyplant.com/celosia/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=January 21, 2021|access-date=2020-12-20|website=Shiny Plant|language=en-US}}</ref> The flowerheads can last up to 8 weeks, and further growth can be promoted by removing dead flowers.<ref name=davegar />

=== Cultivars ===
[[Celosia argentea var. cristata|''Celosia argentea'' var. ''cristata'']] 'Flamingo Feathers' is a cultivar that can grow up to 2 feet in height. The colors are predominantly pink to light violet, and the leaves are a darker green than other cultivars. The Century cultivars are usually taller (1–2 feet), and are bright red, yellow, orange, or pink. The Kimono cultivars are generally smaller (4 inches – 1 foot), and have more muted colors, though similar to the Century cultivars. Other colors, such as white, burgundy, orange-red, etc., can be found. Certain varieties will grow to 3–4 feet in height.<ref name=davegar />
''Celosia plumosa'', also known as Prince of Wales feathers,<ref name="Feathers">{{cite web |url= http://www.gardeninginsouthafrica.co.za/content/view/61/44/ |title= Prince of Wales Feathers – Celosia plumosa |url-status= dead |archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20081210020718/http://www.gardeninginsouthafrica.co.za/content/view/61/44/ |archivedate= 2008-12-10 }}</ref> is a synonym for ''Celosia argentea''. Seeds may be sold as mixtures.

== Uses ==
It is used in Africa to help control the growth of the parasitic ''[[Striga (plant)|Striga]]'' plant. It can also be used in [[soap]]s.<ref name=avrdc>{{cite web|title=Celosia|url=http://avrdc.org/?p=3841|work=AVRDC|accessdate=13 December 2013}}</ref>

===Food===
The leaves and flowers are edible and are grown for such use particularly in west Africa and [[Southeast Asia]].<ref name="prota">{{cite book |last1=Grubben |first1=G.J.H. |last2=Denton |first2=O.A. |year=2004 |title=Plant Resources of Tropical Africa |volume=2. Vegetables |location= Leiden, Netherlands |publisher=ROTA Foundation; Backhuys; CTA }}</ref> ''Celosia argentea'' var. ''argentea'' or "Lagos spinach" is one of the main [[boiled greens]] in [[West Africa]], where it is known as ''soko yòkòtò'' ([[Yoruba language|Yoruba]]) or ''farar áláyyafó'' ([[Hausa language|Hausa]]).<ref>[http://www.echonet.org ECHO]   {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100510115947/http://www.echonet.org/ |date=May 10, 2010 }}</ref><ref>Hanelt ''et al.'', ''Mansfeld's encyclopedia of agricultural and horticultural crops'', 2001 [https://books.google.com/books?id=10IMFSavIMsC&pg=PA265 Google Books]</ref>
